title: Geo-anchoring checkpoints and lockstep failover guardrails for private/VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Private/VPC/on-prem customers require cryptographically verifiable proof that inference workloads executed within an approved geography and that data retention windows were enforced during and after regional failover. Current telemetry surfaces snapshots and logs, but we lack a tamper-resistant, queryable checkpoint format and guardrails that prevent inadvertent cross-region failover or unbounded retention drifts.
goal: Introduce a geo-anchoring checkpoint subsystem (tamper-resistant incremental snapshots + signed attestations) and a lockstep failover controller that enforces regional constraints and retention policies for private/VPC/on-prem deployments. Provide an automated audit export that produces forensics-ready bundles for compliance review.
scope: Implementation covers: 1) checkpoint schema and signing; 2) local ledger + periodic remote attest export; 3) failover precondition checks and lockstep gating; 4) retention window enforcement and drift alerts; 5) developer+operator APIs and Console surfaces to query proofs and export bundles. Not covered: multi-cloud routing policy design (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint artifacts created on all private nodes at configurable intervals and on topology changes; each artifact is signed with customer-specific KMS key and includes node metadata, effective model/version, and retention delta.
Automated export generates a tamper-evident bundle (ledger + checkpoints + audit-log indices) that can be fetched via the customer's control plane and retained per customer's retention policy.

Failover controller rejects or stalls cross-region switchover attempts when preconditions (geo anchoring, retention holdbacks) are not satisfied; operator override is audited and requires two-person approval for customers with 'sovereign' flag.
Console shows per-tenant residency proof timeline and highlights any retention drift or missed checkpoints with direct links to bundles.

E2E tests that simulate node loss, network partition, and emergency switchover verify that no data moves outside allowed geography and that a forensic bundle is produced within SLA (<=15 minutes after event).
Security review completed and KMS/HSM integration validated for signing keys and key rotation flows.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): checkpoint schema design, KMS signing integration, local ledger (append-only), basic Console proof viewer.
Phase 2 (3 sprints): automated export pipeline, tamper-evident bundle format, retention enforcement engine, and API endpoints for bundle retrieval.
Phase 3 (2 sprints): lockstep failover controller, operator override flows, two-person approval integration, and rollout to selected beta tenants.
Phase 4 (1 sprint): hardening, e2e chaos tests, docs, and compliance handover pack for SOC/GDPR reviews.
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint serialization, signing, and verification against rotated keys.
Integration tests: end-to-end creation -> export -> verification of bundle using customer's public key.
Chaos scenarios: simulate regional partition, forced switchover, and verify lockstep gating blocks illegal failover and that forensic bundle is produced within SLA.
Performance: measure checkpointing CPU/memory overhead at 2000 rps on private node and ensure <3% token-latency regression.
Pen test and threat modeling for tamper mechanisms and ledger exposure surface.
audit_artifacts_spec: Bundles are ZIP archives with: signed-ledger.jsonl (append-only ledger entries), checkpoints/<timestamp>.json.gz (signed), logs/index.ndjson (references with offsets), and meta/manifest.json (bundle signature). Each bundle is signed using platform key and includes customer's KMS-signed checkpoint roots. Bundles will be HMACed and stored in immutable customer storage for retention duration.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal infra and SOC team running on dev private cluster; collect early telemetry and refine artifact size limits.
Beta: 3 pilot customers (one on-prem, one VPC, one private cloud) with explicit compliance requirements; enable with monitoring and runbook.
Gradual rollout: enable by feature flag for private deployments; monitor retention alerts and false positives for 2 weeks before broad enabling.
Hard requirement: for customers on Dedicated+Private with 'residency_enforced' tag, enable lockstep gating by default.

open_blockers: Legal review of exported bundle contents for specific regulated industries
notes: Trade-offs discussed: embedding full logs increases bundle size but simplifies forensics; compromise is selective indexing with off-archive on-demand retrieval. We will iterate based on pilot feedback.
customer-facing_summary: For customers with strict geographic and retention needs, this work provides verifiable checkpoints and strict failover gates so the platform can demonstrate where inference ran and that retention rules were obeyed during failover. Exports are formatted for auditors and backed by cryptographic signatures.
